risk_reasons: It removes sign-in from every admin identity on a shared Supabase project — the authorization surface of the whole admin control plane
It uses the service_role key outside any request-scoped gate, and a mis-targeted invocation would revoke the wrong environment's admins
It accompanies the MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED flip, which changes proxy behaviour for admin pages and for enrolled owners
goal: One command REVOKES a RepWorth admin identity — it bans the Supabase Auth login so the identity can no longer sign in, leaves the public.users row and its role='admin' completely intact (users rows are FK targets), writes one admin_revoked row through writeAdminAuditLog, is idempotent, and is fully reversed by --restore. It reuses scripts/mint-admin.ts's environment selection and scripts/staging-guard.ts's assertMintTarget, so production is reachable only behind an explicit --env production selector plus a matching --confirm-ref, exactly like minting.
non_goals: Deleting any row — not public.users, not auth.users, not auth.mfa_factors, not auth.sessions. The owner decision on #1182 is REVOKE, never row deletion
Changing users.role away from 'admin' — the revoke is the Auth-side ban only, so restore is a single reversal
Removing or resetting an admin's MFA factors — that would make --restore non-reversing
Any migration or schema change; admin_audit_log and users are used exactly as migration 117 and 001 define them
Any touch of src/proxy.ts, src/lib/config/ or src/lib/shared/csrf.ts — #1186 owns those files in a parallel worktree
Folding the nine admin GETs onto requireAdminWithAal2 — that is #1184, and ADR 0025 D5 requires it to land AFTER this flag flip
Minting a new admin — scripts/mint-admin.ts owns that verb and is not modified
Any production write of any kind in this run: no revoke, no flag flip, no mint. The production plan is prepared and handed to the owner
user_visible_behavior: An operator runs pnpm tsx scripts/revoke-admin.ts --email <e> --confirm-ref <project-ref> [--env local|staging|production] [--restore] [--dry-run] and the script prints TARGET (project ref, Supabase host, user@host:port database descriptor) before it writes anything
A successful revoke prints REVOKED with the users.id and auth_id, and states that the users row was left in place
A successful restore prints RESTORED with the same identifiers
--dry-run runs every refusal check and the target guard and writes nothing to Postgres or Supabase Auth
Re-running a revoke against an already-banned identity prints ALREADY REVOKED, exits 0 and writes no second audit row; the same holds for --restore against an identity that is not banned
An email with no users row, or a users row whose role is not 'admin', is refused with nothing written

A --confirm-ref that is not exactly the project ref parsed out of BOTH the Supabase URL host and the database connection target is refused before any call; a production project ref is refused outright unless --env production was typed

When the ban succeeds but the audit write fails, the script says the ban COMMITTED, names the audit row that must be recorded by hand, and exits non-zero — it never reports a clean revoke it did not fully record
invariants: Invariant #8 — users.auth_id maps to the Supabase Auth identity, and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY is read only inside this Node script, never by browser code
Invariants #12 and #15 — the script is the composition root: it builds its own postgres and Supabase clients from env and passes them into the domain helpers, which never import @/lib/db/server

admin_audit_log is written ONLY through writeAdminAuditLog (src/lib/audit/log.ts, migration 117) — never a raw INSERT. account_audit_log is impossible for an admin: its account_id is NOT NULL and an admin's account_id is NULL
No row is ever deleted or UPDATEd in public.users; the only Postgres write is the INSERT into admin_audit_log

admin_audit_log.actor_user_id stays NOT NULL and is satisfied without a migration: the revoked admin is its own actor (the self-actor precedent scripts/mint-admin.ts set for admin_minted), because after a full reset there may be NO other admin at all
Production is reachable ONLY behind an explicit --env production selector AND a --confirm-ref equal to the ref parsed from both halves of the target; no mode defaults to production
No new environment variable and no feature flag is introduced by the script
edge_cases: No users row for the email — refuse before any Auth call, nothing written
A users row exists but role is not 'admin' — refuse; this script only revokes admins
The users row has a NULL or empty auth_id (half-2-only identity) — refuse, naming the row, because there is no Auth identity to ban
The identity is already banned and --restore was not passed — report ALREADY REVOKED, exit 0, write no audit row
The identity is not banned and --restore was passed — report ALREADY ACTIVE, exit 0, write no audit row

auth.users is unreadable on the target (the local and CI test databases provision schema auth with no auth.users relation) — the ban-state probe reports unavailable, the run says so, and the transition is attempted anyway; the Auth API is idempotent for a repeated ban
The Auth ban call fails — nothing is written to Postgres and the run exits non-zero; the Auth outcome is reported as UNKNOWN when the failure is a transport failure rather than an API refusal

The audit INSERT fails after the ban committed — the ban STANDS (it is the security-relevant act), the run exits non-zero and prints the exact row an operator must record; it is never reported as a clean revoke
--confirm-ref absent, partial, or matching only one half of a mismatched credential pair — refuse before any call
Email is trimmed and lowercased before every comparison, so casing cannot address the wrong identity
existing_patterns_to_follow: scripts/mint-admin.ts — the composition-root shape, readMintConfig/resolveMintEnv environment selection, describeConnectionTarget/extractProjectRefForLog target description, buildMintGuardInput, the pure formatX report functions, and the self-actor admin_audit_log write
scripts/staging-guard.ts assertMintTarget — the third mode, reused verbatim; no fourth mode is added
scripts/run-direct-cli.ts — the direct-invocation guard that makes importing one CLI module from another safe
scripts/mint-admin.ts probeAuthIdentity — the to_regclass('auth.users') guard for a relation the test databases do not provision
test_seams: revokeAdmin(sql, supabase, input) takes both clients as parameters, so the unit suite drives it with a fake sql template tag and a stubbed supabase.auth.admin
formatRevokeReport(result, target) is pure, so 'never prints a secret' and every operator-facing line are assertions over a value
buildRevokeGuardInput is the tested JOIN between the parsed --env selector and assertMintTarget's allowProduction
tests_to_add: refuses a production-looking target when --env production was not passed
permits a production target only when --env production AND a matching --confirm-ref are both present
refuses when there is no users row for the email, and calls no Auth API
refuses when the users row exists but its role is not admin
refuses when the users row has no auth_id
a --dry-run runs every refusal check and writes nothing to Postgres or Supabase Auth
revoke bans the Auth identity with a ban_duration and never deletes a user
revoke is idempotent: an already-banned identity reports already_revoked and writes no audit row
restore lifts the ban by sending ban_duration none
restore is idempotent: an identity that is not banned reports already_active and writes no audit row
a failed Auth ban writes no audit row and reports failure
an audit write that fails after a committed ban reports the ban as standing and exits non-zero
the report never prints the service key, a password, or a recovery link
revoke writes exactly one admin_revoked row whose actor FK resolves to the revoked admin
restore writes exactly one admin_restored row
neither revoke nor restore deletes or updates the users row
rollback_plan: Every revoke is reversed by the same script with --restore, which lifts the ban and writes an admin_restored row; no row was deleted, so nothing needs re-creating. The MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED flip is reversed by setting the staging variable back to false and redeploying, per the flag-flip skill.
observability: One admin_audit_log row per state transition (admin_revoked / admin_restored) carrying the email, auth_id, ban duration, the self-actor markers, and the unauthenticated-shell operator provenance. The operator-facing report names the TARGET before any write.
required_approvals: Owner go for the MFA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED flip on staging (given 2026-09-08)
Owner merge approval on the PR to main (high-risk lane)
Owner go, command by command, for every production step — none is executed in this run
